newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian banks want privacy for personal acounts.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian banks want privacy for personal acounts.

text.p: The Slovenian Bank Association said on Wednesday it was considering legal action against a government decree extending tax authorities' control over citizens' bank accounts.

The decree, passed by parliament last week, will come into effect in January and will enable tax authorities to check all citizens' bank accounts. Up to now the tax office could only look into business accounts.
"We believe the decree is not in line with the bank law, which proclaims secrecy for all citizens bank accounts except for business ones," Srecko Korber, head of the Bank Association, told Reuters.
"We still have to decide whether to take the matter to the Constitutional Court," Korber added.
Previously tax authorities could only obtain information about citizens' personal tolar and foreign currency accounts with court approval.
Korber said the legislation may encourage a significant number of Slovenians to open bank accounts abroad in order to keep them private.
"Most people don't like their bank accounts to be controlled although they are doing nothing wrong," Korber said. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
